question: We serve a patient who has just suffered a traffic accident. She is conscious and when taking the constants she has a systolic blood pressure of 70 mmHg and a heart rate of 45 beats / minute. In addition, the skin of the extremities is hot. What is the most likely cause of the shock?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Low systolic blood pressure" -> "Bradycardia (heart rate 45 bpm)" -> "Warm extremities" -> "Neurogenic shock" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Low systolic blood pressure" -> "Bradycardia (heart rate 45 bpm)" -> "Warm extremities" -> "Septic shock" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Low systolic blood pressure" -> "Bradycardia (heart rate 45 bpm)" -> "Warm extremities" -> "Hypovolemic shock" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Low systolic blood pressure" -> "Bradycardia (heart rate 45 bpm)" -> "Warm extremities" -> "Intrinsic cardiogenic shock" -> 40%
CHAIN: "Low systolic blood pressure" -> "Bradycardia (heart rate 45 bpm)" -> "Warm extremities" -> "Obstructive cardiogenic shock" -> 30%
analysis: The patient presents with hypotension (systolic blood pressure of 70 mmHg) and bradycardia (heart rate of 45 beats per minute), along with warm extremities. These symptoms are characteristic of neurogenic shock, which can occur due to spinal cord injury often associated with trauma such as a traffic accident. Neurogenic shock is distinguished by the loss of sympathetic tone, leading to vasodilation, hypotension, and bradycardia, with warm skin due to peripheral vasodilation.
